drafted_from: tool row in tools/benchmark-small-local-models/tool-rows.json, do-work/sample_shots_across_groups.py and test/test_benchmark.py (Library)
start_here: Say to your AI: "Sample up to 5 videos from my format library at formats-library, spread over creators, with 10 evenly spaced shots each, and cut a frame for every shot."

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON.

instructions: 1. Pour the two example settings rows into your own list:settings (see pour), or write your own row record:setting:benchmark-small-local-models~person~<you> whose settings hold {"commands":{"sample_shots_across_groups":{...your defaults}}}.
2. Say the line in start_here. Your AI reads this tool's row with tools:list {tool: "tool:sample-shots-and-frames-from-my-format-library"} and gets its run command.

3. Your AI writes the request as a JSON file (request.json), adds settings_record from your settings row if you keep one, and runs python3 trillion-workshop/tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/sample_shots_across_groups.py request.json on your computer.
4. It reads the last line the script prints: {"result": ...} or {"error": "what to change"} (exit code 2), then tells you the result in plain words.

5. Then run cut_sample_frames with the shots it gave, your frame_tool (an `evidence frames` command) and an out_dir; or run sample_candidates_for_slots with slots and exclude_prefix and then cut_candidate_frames.

worked_examples.title: Two videos of two creators sampled, shaped by the video's own size
worked_examples.ask: Pick shots across my format library so I can label their frames.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/sample_shots_across_groups.py and run with test/test_benchmark.py's library (Library.test_shots_are_spread_over_creators_spaced_and_shaped, cut down): library/formats/c1/v1/shots.tsv holds rows 0-2 (wide a-roll, close a-roll, close a-roll, 2 s each) with videos/v1.mp4 = 1080x1920, library/formats/c2/v2/shots.tsv one close b-roll shot 0-2 with videos/v2.mp4 = 1920x1080 turned 90 degrees. request.json = {"library":"library","seed":17,"videos":5,"rounds":2,"big_creator":10,"per_video":10,"min_seconds":0.4,"fields":["size","kind"]}. Run: python3 trillion-workshop/tools/benchmark-small-local-models/do-work/sample_shots_across_groups.py request.json
worked_examples.hands_back: {"result":{"shots":[{"video":"v1","creator":"c1","row":0,"t_mid":1.0,"w":1080,"h":1920,"reference":{"size":"wide","kind":"a-roll"}, ...},{"video":"v1","row":1,"t_mid":3.0,"reference":{"size":"close","kind":"a-roll"}},{"video":"v1","row":2,"t_mid":5.0,...},{"video":"v2","creator":"c2","row":0,"t_mid":1.0,"w":1080,"h":1920,"reference":{"size":"close","kind":"b-roll"}}],"videos":2,"creators":2}}: v2 is stored 1920x1080 but turned 90 degrees, so its shot is read as 1080x1920; each shot keeps its tsv path and its own labels as the reference.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for the same job and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and this kit list as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
